messages:
mike_acme: Hey team, customer hitting streaming disconnects mid-response and sees a 429 after ~12s. They say token rotated client-side during the stream.

sara_support: sorry to hear that, can you paste the stream logs and the client repro?

mike_acme: here's the client behavior: it refreshes creds then sends a resume request to the SSE endpoint with the same session id. sometimes gets 200 resume, sometimes 429 mid-stream. sample curl: `curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <new-token>\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/recv?session=abc123&resume=true\"`

sara_support: got it. customer claims billing shows double token charge when resume succeeds. Lee, tagging for accounting.

lee_billing: can you grab the ledger ids for the two tokens? we need correlation_id from logs.

mike_acme: pasted server log fragment:

```
[2025-11-02T12:01:12Z] conn=78abc session=abc123 token_id=tok-old req=recv resume=true correlation=rc-445
[2025-11-02T12:01:12Z] conn=78abc stream_status=partial tokens_charged=28 ledger_id=L-9001
[2025-11-02T12:01:24Z] conn=af31d session=abc123 token_id=tok-new req=recv resume=true correlation=rc-446
[2025-11-02T12:01:24Z] conn=af31d stream_status=resumed tokens_charged=8 ledger_id=L-9002
[2025-11-02T12:01:24Z] billing: credit L-9001 debited 36, L-9002 debited 8 -> total 44
```

mike_acme: customer expected only the new tokens to be debited (8), not double-counting previous partial (28).

jamie_eng: interesting — looks like session affinity leaked across connection ids but both ledgers got charged. can you confirm where resume logic ties charges to a ledger?

sara_support: customer says client increments before resume, then continues producing tokens. the partial chunk got billed, then resume billed again.

jamie_eng: quick hypothesis: when resume=true, runtime honors prior session's kv-cache but doesn't reassign ledger pointer; it continues to charge the original ledger, but because token bound to new auth header, our accounting service creates a new ledger and charges both. need repro steps.

ops-bot: ACTION_CREATED: ticket INC-2025 assigned to jamie_eng (priority: high)

lee_billing: repro accepted. ledger L-9001 shows tokens from connection 78abc then L-9002 created for new token. Looks like a race where resume handshake completes after the billing attribution window.

jamie_eng: can you run this reproducible sequence and capture these headers?

1) open SSE with token-A, start generation (~30 tokens)
2) client does token refresh and immediately issues resume with token-B and same session id
3) force the server to accept resume on a new connection (simulate network drop)

Use this test CLI (customer used Node but here's curl):

```
# open initial stream (token A)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer tokenA" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/recv?session=abc123&resume=false" > /dev/null &
# after ~10s, rotate token locally
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer tokenB" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/recv?session=abc123&resume=true"
```

jamie_eng: capture server headers: X-Correlation, X-Ledger, Conn-ID. I suspect resume currently spins up a new ledger until the atomic transfer completes.

mike_acme: shared a quick repro log from customer with correlation headers.

```
rcid: rc-446 X-Ledger: L-9002 X-Conn: af31d
rcid: rc-445 X-Ledger: L-9001 X-Conn: 78abc
```

jamie_eng: thanks. prioritizing a short-term mitigation: avoid using resume across token rotations — recommend clients reconnect fresh (resume=false) until we patch. I'll add a server-side guard to delay creating a new ledger until resume handshake finishes.

lee_billing: for affected invoices we can issue an adjustment once engineering confirms the root cause. please attach impacted account ids.

mike_acme: customer accepted workaround (reconnect after refresh). asked for ETA on patch.

jamie_eng: ETA: patch to make ledger attribution atomic for resume flows — aiming for a week; will push hotfix to staging for immediate verification.

sara_support: I'll update the support ticket with repro, mitigation, and billing next steps. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
